tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();

43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`

50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error

52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

schema.name: Agent
schema.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.
56	
57	## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
58	- Check your files only:
59	    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
60	    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
61	  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
62	- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
63	  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
64	  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
65	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
66	  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
67	- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
68	  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.
69	
70	## Git
71	- Work and commit on your branch (already created for your worktree). Small logical commits,
72	  message style: `refactor(<area>): <what>` or `test(<area>): <what>`. Each message ends with:
73	    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
74	- Commit only your files. Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not run `git reset --hard`
75	  or any command that touches other worktrees.
76	
77	## Final report (your last message, at most 40 lines)
78	- Files changed; commit list (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`).
79	- Signature changes (name: old -> new).
80	- Test inventory: number of test functions before (`git show 7e36233:<file> | grep -cE '#\[(motsu::)?test\]'`)
81	  and after, per file; any test you merged or removed (with reason).
82	- Compile status of your files (lib / tests); whether the crate compiled as a whole at the time.
83	- Requests to other owners; blockers; anything you were unsure about.
84

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error

27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.

34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())

46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).

321	    /// Sets a `value` number of tokens as the allowance of `spender` over the
322	    /// caller's tokens.
323	    ///
324	    /// Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded.
325	    /// # Arguments
326	    ///
327	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
328	    /// * `owner` - Account that owns the tokens.
329	    /// * `spender` - Account that will spend the tokens.
330	    /// * `emit_event` - Emit an [`Approval`] event flag.
331	    ///
332	    /// # Errors
333	    ///
334	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSpender`] - If the `spender` address is
335	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
336	    ///
337	    /// # Events
338	    ///
339	    /// * [`Approval`].
340	    fn _approve(
341	        &mut self,
342	        owner: Address,
343	        spender: Address,
344	        value: U256,
345	        emit_event: bool,
346	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
347	        if owner.is_zero() {
348	            return Err(Error::InvalidApprover(ERC20InvalidApprover {
349	                approver: Address::ZERO}));
350	        }
351	
352	        if spender.is_zero() {
353	            return Err(Error::InvalidSpender(ERC20InvalidSpender {
354	                spender: Address::ZERO}));
355	        }
356	
357	        self.allowances.setter(owner).insert(spender, value);
358	        if emit_event {
359	            self.vm().log(Approval { owner, spender, value });
360	        }
361	        Ok(true)
362	    }
363	
364	    /// Internal implementation of transferring tokens between two accounts.
365	    ///
366	    /// # Arguments
367	    ///
368	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
369	    /// * `from` - Account to transfer tokens from.
370	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
371	    /// * `value` - The number of tokens to transfer.
372	    ///
373	    /// # Errors
374	    ///
375	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If the `from` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
376	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `to` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
377	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
378	    ///   enough tokens.
379	    ///
380	    /// # Events
381	    ///
382	    /// * [`Transfer`].
383	    fn _transfer(
384	        &mut self,
385	        from: Address,
386	        to: Address,
387	        value: U256,
388	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
389	        if from.is_zero() {
390	            return Err(Error::InvalidSender(ERC20InvalidSender {
391	                sender: Address::ZERO}));
392	        }
393	        if to.is_zero() {
394	            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiver(ERC20InvalidReceiver {
395	                receiver: Address::ZERO}));
396	        }
397	
398	        self._update(from, to, value)?;
399	
400	        Ok(())
401	    }
402	
403	    /// Creates a `value` amount of tokens and assigns them to `account`,
404	    /// by transferring it from [`Address::ZERO`].
405	    ///
406	    /// # Errors
407	    ///
408	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `account` address is
409	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
410	    ///
411	    /// # Events
412	    ///
413	    /// * [`Transfer`].
414	    ///
415	    /// # Panics
416	    ///
417	    /// * If `total_supply` exceeds [`U256::MAX`].
418	    pub fn _mint(
419	        &mut self,
420	        account: Address,
421	        value: U256,
422	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
423	        if account.is_zero() {
424	            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiver(ERC20InvalidReceiver {
425	                receiver: Address::ZERO}));
426	        }
427	        self._update(Address::ZERO, account, value)
428	    }
429	
430	    /// Transfers a `value` amount of tokens from `from` to `to`, or
431	    /// alternatively mints (or burns) if `from` (or `to`) is the zero address.
432	    ///
433	    /// All customizations to transfers, mints, and burns should be done by
434	    /// using this function.
435	    ///
436	    /// # Arguments
437	    ///
438	    /// * `from` - Owner's address.
439	    /// * `to` - Recipient's address.
440	    /// * `value` - Amount to be transferred.
441	    ///
442	    /// # Errors
443	    ///
444	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
445	    ///   enough tokens.
446	    ///
447	    /// # Events
448	    ///
449	    /// * [`Transfer`].
450	    ///
451	    /// # Panics
452	    ///
453	    /// * If `total_supply` exceeds [`U256::MAX`]. It may happen during `mint`
454	    ///   operation.
455	    pub fn _update(
456	        &mut self,
457	        from: Address,
458	        to: Address,
459	        value: U256,
460	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
461	        if from.is_zero() {
462	            // Mint operation. Overflow check required: the rest of the code
463	            // assumes that `total_supply` never overflows.
464	            self.total_supply.add_assign_checked(
465	                value,
466	                "should not exceed `U256::MAX` for `total_supply`",
467	            );
468	        } else {
469	            let from_balance = self.balances.get(from);
470	            if from_balance < value {
471	                return Err(Error::InsufficientBalance(
472	                    ERC20InsufficientBalance {
473	                        sender: from,
474	                        balance: from_balance,
475	                        needed: value},
476	                ));
477	            }
478	            // Overflow not possible:
479	            // `value` <= `from_balance` <= `total_supply`.
480	            self.balances.setter(from).set(from_balance - value);
481	        }
482	
483	        if to.is_zero() {
484	            // Overflow not possible:
485	            // `value` <= `total_supply` or
486	            // `value` <= `from_balance` <= `total_supply`.
487	            self.total_supply.sub_assign_unchecked(value);
488	        } else {
489	            // Overflow not possible:
490	            // `balance_to` + `value` is at most `total_supply`,
491	            // which fits into a `U256`.
492	            self.balances.setter(to).add_assign_unchecked(value);
493	        }
494	
495	        self.vm().log(Transfer { from, to, value });
496	
497	        Ok(())
498	    }
499	
500	    /// Destroys a `value` amount of tokens from `account`,
501	    /// lowering the total supply.
502	    ///
503	    /// # Arguments
504	    ///
505	    /// * `account` - Owner's address.
506	    /// * `value` - Amount to be burnt.
507	    ///
508	    /// # Errors
509	    ///
510	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If the `from` address is [`Address::ZERO`].
511	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If the `from` address doesn't have
512	    ///   enough tokens.
513	    ///
514	    /// # Events
515	    ///
516	    /// * [`Transfer`].
517	    pub fn _burn(
518	        &mut self,
519	        account: Address,
520	        value: U256,
521	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
522	        if account == Address::ZERO {
523	            return Err(Error::InvalidSender(ERC20InvalidSender {
524	                sender: Address::ZERO}));
525	        }
526	        self._update(account, Address::ZERO, value)
527	    }
528	
529	    /// Updates `owner`'s allowance for `spender` based on spent `value`.
530	    ///
531	    /// Does not update the allowance value in the case of infinite allowance.
532	    ///
533	    /// # Arguments
534	    ///
535	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
536	    /// * `owner` - Account to transfer tokens from.
537	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
538	    /// * `value` - The number of tokens to transfer.
539	    ///
540	    /// # Errors
541	    ///
542	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientAllowance`] - If not enough allowance is
543	    ///   available.
544	    ///
545	    /// # Events
546	    ///
547	    /// * [`Approval`].
548	    pub fn _spend_allowance(
549	        &mut self,
550	        owner: Address,
551	        spender: Address,
552	        value: U256,
553	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
554	        let current_allowance = self.allowance(owner, spender);
555	        if current_allowance != U256::MAX {
556	            if current_allowance < value {
557	                return Err(Error::InsufficientAllowance(
558	                    ERC20InsufficientAllowance {
559	                        spender,
560	                        allowance: current_allowance,
561	                        needed: value},
562	                ));
563	            }
564	
565	            self._approve(owner, spender, current_allowance - value, false)?;
566	        }
567	
568	        Ok(())
569	    }
570	}

1	//! Permit Contract.
2	//!
3	//! Extension of the ERC-20 standard allowing approvals to be made
4	//! via signatures, as defined in the [ERC].
5	//!
6	//! Adds the `permit` method, which can be used to change an account’s
7	//! ERC20 allowance (see [`crate::token::erc20::IErc20::allowance`])
8	//! by presenting a message signed by the account.
9	//! By not relying on [`erc20::IErc20::approve`],
10	//! the token holder account doesn’t need to send a transaction,
11	//! and thus is not required to hold Ether at all.
12	//!
13	//! [ERC]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612
14	
15	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
16	
17	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, keccak256, Address, B256, U256, U8};
18	use alloy_sol_types::SolType;
19	use stylus_sdk::{stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError, function_selector, prelude::*};
20	
21	use crate::{
22	    token::erc20::{self, Erc20},
23	    utils::{
24	        cryptography::eip712::IEip712,
25	        nonces::{INonces, Nonces},
26	        precompiles::{
27	            primitives::ecrecover::{
28	                self, ECDSAInvalidSignature, ECDSAInvalidSignatureS},
29	            Precompiles}}};
30	
31	const PERMIT_TYPEHASH: [u8; 32] =
32	    keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
33	        .update(b"Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)")
34	        .finalize();
35	
36	pub use sol::*;
37	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
38	mod sol {
39	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
40	
41	    pub(crate) type StructHashTuple = sol! {
42	        tuple(bytes32, address, address, uint256, uint256, uint256)
43	    };
44	
45	    sol! {
46	        /// Indicates an error related to the fact that
47	        /// permit deadline has expired.
48	        #[derive(Debug)]
49	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
50	        error ERC2612ExpiredSignature(uint256 deadline);
51	
52	        /// Indicates an error related to the issue about mismatched signature.
53	        #[derive(Debug)]
54	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
55	        error ERC2612InvalidSigner(address signer, address owner);
56	    }
57	}
58	
59	/// A Permit error.
60	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
61	pub enum Error {
62	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that
63	    /// permit deadline has expired.
64	    ExpiredSignature(ERC2612ExpiredSignature),
65	    /// Indicates an error related to the issue about mismatched signature.
66	    InvalidSigner(ERC2612InvalidSigner),
67	    /// Indicates an error related to the current balance of `sender`. Used in
68	    /// transfers.
69	    InsufficientBalance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientBalance),
70	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
71	    InvalidSender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSender),
72	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
73	    InvalidReceiver(erc20::ERC20InvalidReceiver),
74	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender`’s `allowance`. Used in
75	    /// transfers.
76	    InsufficientAllowance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientAllowance),
77	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender` to be approved. Used in
78	    /// approvals.
79	    InvalidSpender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSpender),
80	    /// Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used
81	    /// in approvals. approver Address initiating an approval operation.
82	    InvalidApprover(erc20::ERC20InvalidApprover),
83	    /// The signature derives the [`Address::ZERO`].
84	    InvalidSignature(ECDSAInvalidSignature),
85	    /// The signature has an `S` value that is in the upper half order.
86	    InvalidSignatureS(ECDSAInvalidSignatureS)}
87	
88	impl From<erc20::Error> for Error {
89	    fn from(value: erc20::Error) -> Self {
90	        match value {

221	        spender: Address,
222	        value: U256,
223	        deadline: U256,
224	        v: u8,
225	        r: B256,
226	        s: B256,

249	        }

251	        erc20._approve(owner, spender, value, true)?;

166	/// Interface of the ERC-3156 Flash Lender, as defined in [ERC-3156].
167	///
168	/// [ERC-3156]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3156
169	#[interface_id]
170	#[public]
171	pub trait IErc3156FlashLender {
172	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
173	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
174	
175	    /// Returns the maximum amount of tokens available for loan.
176	    ///
177	    /// NOTE: This function does not consider any form of supply cap, so in case
178	    /// it's used in a token with a cap like
179	    /// [`crate::token::erc20::extensions::Capped`], make sure to override this
180	    /// function to integrate the cap instead of [`U256::MAX`].
181	    ///
182	    /// # Arguments
183	    ///
184	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
185	    /// * `token` - The address of the token that is requested.
186	    #[must_use]
187	    fn max_flash_loan(&self, token: Address) -> U256;
188	
189	    /// Returns the fee applied when doing flash loans.
190	    ///
191	    /// # Arguments
192	    ///
193	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
194	    /// * `token` - The token to be flash loaned.
195	    /// * `value` - The amount of tokens to be loaned.
196	    ///
197	    /// # Errors
198	    ///
199	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If the token is not supported.
200	    ///
201	    /// # Examples
202	    ///
203	    /// ```rust,ignore
204	    /// fn flash_fee(&self, token: Address, value: U256) -> Result<U256, flash_mint::Error> {
205	    ///     self.erc20_flash_mint.flash_fee(token, value)
206	    /// }
207	    /// ```
208	    fn flash_fee(
209	        &self,
210	        token: Address,
211	        value: U256,
212	    ) -> Result<U256, Self::Error>;
213	
214	    /// Performs a flash loan.
215	    ///
216	    /// New tokens are minted and sent to the `receiver`, who is required to
217	    /// implement the [`IERC3156FlashBorrower`] interface. By the end of the
218	    /// flash loan, the receiver is expected to own value + fee tokens and have
219	    /// them approved back to the token contract itself so they can be burned.
220	    ///
221	    /// Returns a boolean value indicating whether the operation succeeded.
222	    ///
223	    /// # Arguments
224	    ///
225	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
226	    /// * `receiver` - The receiver of the flash loan. Should implement the
227	    ///   [`IERC3156FlashBorrower::on_flash_loan`] interface.
228	    /// * `token` - The token to be flash loaned. Only [`self.vm().contract_address()`]
229	    ///   is supported.
230	    /// * `value` - The amount of tokens to be loaned.
231	    /// * `data` - Arbitrary data that is passed to the receiver.
232	    ///
233	    /// # Errors
234	    ///
235	    /// * [`Error::ExceededMaxLoan`] - If the `value` is greater than the value
236	    ///   returned by [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`].
237	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If `token` is not supported.
238	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `token` address is not a contract
239	    ///   , the contract fails to execute the call, or the receiver does not
240	    ///   return [`BORROWER_CALLBACK_VALUE`].
241	    ///
242	    /// # Events
243	    ///
244	    /// * [`erc20::Transfer`].
245	    /// * [`erc20::Approval`].
246	    ///
247	    /// # Panics
248	    ///
249	    /// * If the new (temporary) total supply exceeds [`U256::MAX`].
250	    /// * If the sum of the loan value and fee exceeds the maximum value of
251	    ///   [`U256::MAX`].
252	    fn flash_loan(
253	        &mut self,
254	        receiver: Address,
255	        token: Address,
256	        value: U256,
257	        data: Bytes,
258	    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error>;
259	}

261	impl Erc20FlashMint {
262	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::max_flash_loan`].
263	    #[must_use]
264	    pub fn max_flash_loan(&self, token: Address, erc20: &erc20::Erc20) -> U256 {
265	        if token == self.vm().contract_address() {
266	            U256::MAX - erc20.total_supply()
267	        } else {
268	            U256::MIN
269	        }
270	    }
271	
272	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_fee`].
273	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
274	    pub fn flash_fee(
275	        &self,
276	        token: Address,
277	        _value: U256,
278	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
279	        if token == self.vm().contract_address() {
280	            Ok(self.flash_fee_value.get())
281	        } else {
282	            Err(Error::UnsupportedToken(ERC3156UnsupportedToken { token }))
283	        }
284	    }
285	
286	    // This function can reenter, but it doesn't pose a risk because it always
287	    // preserves the property that the amount minted at the beginning is always
288	    // recovered and burned at the end, or else the entire function will revert.
289	    /// See [`IErc3156FlashLender::flash_loan`].
290	    #[allow(clippy::missing_panics_doc, clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
291	    pub fn flash_loan(
292	        &mut self,
293	        receiver: Address,
294	        token: Address,
295	        value: U256,
296	        data: &Bytes,
297	        erc20: &mut Erc20,
298	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
299	        let max_loan = self.max_flash_loan(token, erc20);
300	        if value > max_loan {
301	            return Err(Error::ExceededMaxLoan(ERC3156ExceededMaxLoan {
302	                max_loan}));
303	        }
304	
305	        let fee = self.flash_fee(token, value)?;
306	        if !Address::has_code(&receiver) {
307	            return Err(Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(
308	                ERC3156InvalidReceiver { receiver },
309	            ));
310	        }
311	        erc20._mint(receiver, value)?;
312	        let loan_receiver = IERC3156FlashBorrower::new(receiver);
313	        let loan_return = loan_receiver
314	            .on_flash_loan(
315	                Call::new_in(self),
316	                self.vm().msg_sender(),
317	                token,
318	                value,
319	                fee,
320	                data.to_vec().into(),
321	            )
322	            .map_err(|_| {
323	                Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(ERC3156InvalidReceiver {
324	                    receiver})
325	            })?;
326	        if loan_return != BORROWER_CALLBACK_VALUE {
327	            return Err(Error::ERC3156InvalidReceiver(
328	                ERC3156InvalidReceiver { receiver },
329	            ));
330	        }
331	
332	        let allowance = value
333	            .checked_add(fee)
334	            .expect("allowance should not exceed `U256::MAX`");
335	        erc20._spend_allowance(receiver, self.vm().contract_address(), allowance)?;
336	
337	        let flash_fee_receiver = self.flash_fee_receiver_address.get();
338	
339	        if fee.is_zero() || flash_fee_receiver.is_zero() {
340	            erc20._burn(receiver, allowance)?;
341	        } else {
342	            erc20._burn(receiver, value)?;
343	            erc20._transfer(receiver, flash_fee_receiver, fee)?;
344	        }
345	
346	        Ok(true)
347	    }
348	}

1	//! Wrappers around ERC-20 operations that throw on failure (when the token
2	//! contract returns false).
3	//!
4	//! Tokens that return no value (and instead revert or
5	//! throw on failure) are also supported, non-reverting calls are assumed to be
6	//! successful.
7	//!
8	//! To use this library, you can add a `#[implements(ISafeErc20<Error =
9	//! Error>)]` attribute to your contract, which allows you to call the safe
10	//! operations as `contract.safe_transfer(token_addr, ...)`, etc.
11

96	#[storage]
97	pub struct SafeErc20;

100	/// calling other contracts and not `&mut (impl TopLevelStorage +
101	/// BorrowMut<Self>)`. Should be fixed in the future by the Stylus team.

104	/// Required interface of a [`SafeErc20`] utility contract.
105	#[interface_id]
106	#[public]
107	pub trait ISafeErc20 {
108	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
109	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
110	
111	    /// Transfer `value` amount of `token` from the calling contract to `to`. If
112	    /// `token` returns no value, non-reverting calls are assumed to be
113	    /// successful.
114	    ///
115	    /// # Arguments
116	    ///
117	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
118	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
119	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
120	    /// * `value` - Number of tokens to transfer.
121	    ///
122	    /// # Errors
123	    ///
124	    ///  * [`Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If the `token` address is not a
125	    ///    contract , the contract fails to execute the call or the call returns
126	    ///    value that is not `true`.
127	    fn safe_transfer(
128	        &mut self,
129	        token: Address,
130	        to: Address,
131	        value: U256,
132	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
133	
134	    /// Transfer `value` amount of `token` from `from` to `to`, spending the
135	    /// approval given by `from` to the calling contract. If `token` returns
136	    /// no value, non-reverting calls are assumed to be successful.
137	    ///
138	    /// # Arguments
139	    ///
140	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
141	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
142	    /// * `from` - Account to transfer tokens from.
143	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
144	    /// * `value` - Number of tokens to transfer.
145	    ///
146	    /// # Errors
147	    ///
148	    ///  * [`Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If the `token` address is not a
149	    ///    contract , the contract fails to execute the call or the call returns
150	    ///    value that is not `true`.
151	    fn safe_transfer_from(
152	        &mut self,
153	        token: Address,
154	        from: Address,
155	        to: Address,
156	        value: U256,
157	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
158	
159	    /// Variant of [`Self::safe_transfer`] that returns a `bool` instead of
160	    /// reverting if the operation is not successful.
161	    ///
162	    /// # Arguments
163	    ///
164	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
165	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
166	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
167	    /// * `value` - Number of tokens to transfer.
168	    fn try_safe_transfer(
169	        &mut self,
170	        token: Address,
171	        to: Address,
172	        value: U256,
173	    ) -> bool;
174	
175	    /// Variant of [`Self::safe_transfer_from`] that returns a `bool` instead of
176	    /// reverting if the operation is not successful.
177	    ///
178	    /// # Arguments
179	    ///
180	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
181	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
182	    /// * `from` - Account to transfer tokens from.
183	    /// * `to` - Account to transfer tokens to.
184	    /// * `value` - Number of tokens to transfer.
185	    fn try_safe_transfer_from(
186	        &mut self,
187	        token: Address,
188	        from: Address,
189	        to: Address,
190	        value: U256,
191	    ) -> bool;
192	
193	    /// Increase the calling contract's allowance toward `spender` by `value`.
194	    /// If `token` returns no value, non-reverting calls are assumed to be
195	    /// successful.
196	    ///
197	    /// # Arguments
198	    ///

560	    /// Imitates a Stylus high-level call, relaxing the requirement on the
561	    /// return value: if data is returned, it must not be `false`, otherwise
562	    /// calls are assumed to be successful.
563	    ///
564	    /// # Arguments
565	    ///
566	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
567	    /// * `call` - [`IErc20`] call that implements [`SolCall`] trait.
568	    ///
569	    /// # Errors
570	    ///
571	    /// * [`Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If the `token` address is not a
572	    ///   contract, the contract fails to execute the call or the call returns
573	    ///   value that is not `true`.
574	    fn call_optional_return(
575	        token: Address,
576	        call: &impl SolCall,
577	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
578	        if !token.has_code() {
579	            return Err(Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation(
580	                SafeErc20FailedOperation { token },
581	            ));
582	        }
583	
584	        let result = unsafe {
585	            RawCall::new()
586	                .limit_return_data(0, BOOL_TYPE_SIZE)
587	                .flush_storage_cache()
588	                .call(token, &call.abi_encode())
589	        };
590	
591	        match result {
592	            Ok(data)
593	                if data.is_empty()
594	                    || Bool::abi_decode(&data, true)
595	                        .is_ok_and(|success| success) =>
596	            {
597	                Ok(())
598	            }
599	            _ => Err(SafeErc20FailedOperation { token }.into())}
600	    }
601	
602	    /// Returns the remaining number of ERC-20 tokens that `spender`
603	    /// will be allowed to spend on behalf of an owner.
604	    ///
605	    /// # Arguments
606	    ///
607	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
608	    /// * `token` - Address of the ERC-20 token contract.
609	    /// * `spender` - Account that will spend the tokens.
610	    ///
611	    /// # Errors
612	    ///
613	    /// * [`Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If the contract fails to read
614	    ///   `spender`'s allowance.
615	    fn allowance(
616	        &self,
617	        token: Address,
618	        spender: Address,
619	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
620	        if !Address::has_code(&token) {
621	            return Err(SafeErc20FailedOperation { token }.into());
622	        }
623	
624	        let erc20 = Erc20Interface::new(token);
625	        erc20.allowance(self, self.vm().contract_address(), spender).map_err(|_e| {
626	            Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation(SafeErc20FailedOperation { token })
627	        })
628	    }
629	}

1	//! ERC-4626 Tokenized Vault Standard Implementation as defined in [ERC-4626].
2	//!
3	//! This extension allows the minting and burning of "shares" (represented using
4	//! the ERC-20 inheritance) in exchange for underlying "assets" through
5	//! standardized `deposit`, `mint`, `redeem` and `burn` workflows. This contract
6	//! extends the ERC-20 standard. Any additional extensions included along it
7	//! would affect the "shares" token represented by this contract and not the
8	//! "assets" token which is an independent contract.
9

24	        Erc20, IErc20},
25	    utils::math::alloy::{Math, Rounding}};

34	    sol! {
35	        /// Emitted when assets are deposited into the contract.
36	        #[derive(Debug)]
37	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
38	        event Deposit(address indexed sender, address indexed owner, uint256 assets, uint256 shares);
39	
40	        /// Emitted when assets are withdrawn from the contract.
41	        #[derive(Debug)]
42	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
43	        event Withdraw(
44	            address indexed sender,
45	            address indexed receiver,
46	            address indexed owner,
47	            uint256 assets,
48	            uint256 shares
49	        );
50	    }
51	
52	    sol! {
53	        /// Indicates an attempt to deposit more assets than the max amount for
54	        /// `receiver`.
55	        ///
56	        /// * `receiver` - Address of the asset's recipient.
57	        /// * `assets` - Amount of assets deposited.
58	        /// * `max` - Maximum amount of assets that can be deposited.
59	        #[derive(Debug)]
60	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
61	        error ERC4626ExceededMaxDeposit(address receiver, uint256 assets, uint256 max);
62	
63	        /// Indicates an attempt to mint more shares than the max amount for
64	        /// `receiver`.
65	        ///
66	        /// * `receiver` - Address of share's recipient.
67	        /// * `shares` - Amount of shares to mint.
68	        /// * `max` - Maximum amount of shares that can be minted.
69	        #[derive(Debug)]
70	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
71	        error ERC4626ExceededMaxMint(address receiver, uint256 shares, uint256 max);
72	
73	        /// Indicates an attempt to withdraw more assets than the max amount for
74	        /// `owner`.
75	        ///
76	        /// * `owner` - Address of the asset's owner.
77	        /// * `assets` - Amount of assets to withdraw.
78	        /// * `max` - Maximum amount of assets that can be withdrawn.
79	        #[derive(Debug)]
80	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
81	        error ERC4626ExceededMaxWithdraw(address owner, uint256 assets, uint256 max);
82	
83	        /// Indicates an attempt to redeem more shares than the max amount for
84	        /// `owner`.
85	        ///
86	        /// * `owner` - Address of the share's owner.
87	        /// * `shares` - Amount of shares to redeem.
88	        /// * `max` - Maximum amount of shares that can be redeemed.
89	        #[derive(Debug)]
90	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
91	        error ERC4626ExceededMaxRedeem(address owner, uint256 shares, uint256 max);
92	
93	        /// The address is not a valid ERC-20 token.
94	        ///
95	        /// * `asset` - Address of the invalid ERC-20 token.
96	        #[derive(Debug)]
97	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
98	        error InvalidAsset(address asset);
99	    }

102	/// An [`Erc4626`] error.
103	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
104	pub enum Error {
105	    /// Indicates an attempt to deposit more assets than the max amount for
106	    /// `receiver`.
107	    ExceededMaxDeposit(ERC4626ExceededMaxDeposit),
108	    /// Indicates an attempt to mint more shares than the max amount for
109	    /// `receiver`.
110	    ExceededMaxMint(ERC4626ExceededMaxMint),
111	    /// Indicates an attempt to withdraw more assets than the max amount for
112	    /// `owner`.
113	    ExceededMaxWithdraw(ERC4626ExceededMaxWithdraw),
114	    /// Indicates an attempt to redeem more shares than the max amount for
115	    /// `owner`.
116	    ExceededMaxRedeem(ERC4626ExceededMaxRedeem),
117	    /// The address is not a valid ERC-20 token.
118	    InvalidAsset(InvalidAsset),
119	    /// An operation with an ERC-20 token failed.
120	    SafeErc20FailedOperation(safe_erc20::SafeErc20FailedOperation),
121	    /// Indicates a failed [`ISafeErc20::safe_decrease_allowance`] request.
122	    SafeErc20FailedDecreaseAllowance(
123	        safe_erc20::SafeErc20FailedDecreaseAllowance,
124	    ),
125	    /// Indicates an error related to the current balance of `sender`. Used in
126	    /// transfers.
127	    InsufficientBalance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientBalance),
128	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
129	    InvalidSender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSender),
130	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
131	    InvalidReceiver(erc20::ERC20InvalidReceiver),
132	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender`’s `allowance`. Used in
133	    /// transfers.
134	    InsufficientAllowance(erc20::ERC20InsufficientAllowance),
135	    /// Indicates a failure with the `spender` to be approved. Used in
136	    /// approvals.
137	    InvalidSpender(erc20::ERC20InvalidSpender),
138	    /// Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used
139	    /// in approvals. approver Address initiating an approval operation.
140	    InvalidApprover(erc20::ERC20InvalidApprover)}
141	
142	impl From<safe_erc20::Error> for Error {
143	    fn from(value: safe_erc20::Error) -> Self {
144	        match value {
145	            safe_erc20::Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation(e) => {
146	                Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation(e)
147	            }
148	            safe_erc20::Error::SafeErc20FailedDecreaseAllowance(e) => {
149	                Error::SafeErc20FailedDecreaseAllowance(e)
150	            }
151	        }
152	    }
153	}
154	
155	impl From<erc20::Error> for Error {
156	    fn from(value: erc20::Error) -> Self {
157	        match value {
158	            erc20::Error::InsufficientBalance(e) => {
159	                Error::InsufficientBalance(e)
160	            }
161	            erc20::Error::InvalidSender(e) => Error::InvalidSender(e),
162	            erc20::Error::InvalidReceiver(e) => Error::InvalidReceiver(e),
163	            erc20::Error::InsufficientAllowance(e) => {
164	                Error::InsufficientAllowance(e)
165	            }
166	            erc20::Error::InvalidSpender(e) => Error::InvalidSpender(e),
167	            erc20::Error::InvalidApprover(e) => Error::InvalidApprover(e)}
168	    }
169	}
170	
171	impl MethodError for Error {
172	    fn encode(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
173	        self.into()
174	    }
175	}

866	    /// NOTE: To expose this function in your contract's ABI, implement it as
867	    /// shown in the Examples section below. The implementation should forward

870	    /// # Arguments

884	    ///     }
885	    /// ```

894	    /// Converts a given amount of assets to shares using the specified
895	    /// `rounding` mode.
896	    ///
897	    /// # Arguments
898	    ///
899	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
900	    /// * `assets` - The amount of assets to convert.
901	    /// * `rounding` - The [`Rounding`] mode to use for the conversion.
902	    /// * `erc20` - Read access to an [`Erc20`] contract.
903	    ///
904	    /// # Errors
905	    ///
906	    /// * [`Error::InvalidAsset`] - If the token address is not a valid ERC-20
907	    ///   token.
908	    ///
909	    /// # Panics
910	    ///
911	    /// * If decimal offset calculation overflows in the power operation.
912	    /// * If multiplication or division operations overflow during conversion.
913	    pub fn _convert_to_shares(
914	        &self,
915	        assets: U256,
916	        rounding: Rounding,
917	        erc20: &Erc20,
918	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
919	        let total_supply = erc20.total_supply();
920	
921	        let multiplier = total_supply
922	            .checked_add(
923	                TEN.checked_pow(U256::from(self._decimals_offset())).expect(
924	                    "decimal offset overflow in `Erc4626::_convert_to_shares`",
925	                ),
926	            )
927	            .expect("multiplier overflow in `Erc4626::_convert_to_shares`");
928	
929	        let denominator = self
930	            .total_assets()?
931	            .checked_add(ONE)
932	            .expect("denominator overflow in `Erc4626::_convert_to_shares`");
933	
934	        let shares = assets.mul_div(multiplier, denominator, rounding);
935	
936	        Ok(shares)
937	    }

984	    /// Deposit/mint common workflow.
985	    ///
986	    /// # Arguments
987	    ///
988	    /// * `caller` - Address initiating the deposit.
989	    /// * `receiver` - Address receiving the minted shares.
990	    /// * `assets` - Amount of underlying tokens to transfer.
991	    /// * `shares` - Amount of shares to mint.
992	    /// * `erc20` - Write access to an [`Erc20`] contract.
993	    ///
994	    /// # Errors
995	    ///
996	    /// * [`safe_erc20::Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If token transfer
997	    ///   fails.
998	    /// * [`erc20::Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `receiver` is
999	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
1000	    ///
1001	    /// # Events
1002	    ///
1003	    /// * [`Deposit`]
1004	    pub fn _deposit(
1005	        &mut self,
1006	        caller: Address,
1007	        receiver: Address,
1008	        assets: U256,
1009	        shares: U256,
1010	        erc20: &mut Erc20,
1011	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
1012	        // If asset() is ERC-777, `transfer_from` can trigger a reentrancy
1013	        // BEFORE the transfer happens through the `tokens_to_send` hook. On the
1014	        // other hand, the `token_received` hook, that is triggered after the
1015	        // transfer, calls the vault, which is assumed not malicious.
1016	        //
1017	        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer before we mint so that any
1018	        // reentrancy would happen before the assets are transferred and before
1019	        // the shares are minted, which is a valid state.
1020	
1021	        self.safe_erc20.safe_transfer_from(
1022	            self.asset(),
1023	            caller,
1024	            self.vm().contract_address(),
1025	            assets,
1026	        )?;
1027	
1028	        erc20._mint(receiver, shares)?;
1029	
1030	        self.vm().log(Deposit { sender: caller, owner: receiver, assets, shares });
1031	
1032	        Ok(())
1033	    }

1035	    /// Withdraw/redeem common workflow.
1036	    ///
1037	    /// # Arguments
1038	    ///
1039	    /// * `caller` - Address initiating the withdrawal.
1040	    /// * `receiver` - Address receiving the assets.
1041	    /// * `owner` - Address owning the shares.
1042	    /// * `assets` - Amount of underlying tokens to transfer.
1043	    /// * `shares` - Amount of shares to burn.
1044	    /// * `erc20` - Write access to an [`Erc20`] contract.
1045	    ///
1046	    /// # Errors
1047	    ///
1048	    /// * [`erc20::Error::InsufficientAllowance`] - If `caller` needs allowance.
1049	    /// * [`erc20::Error::InvalidApprover`] - If `owner` is [`Address::ZERO`].
1050	    /// * [`erc20::Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If `owner` lacks shares.
1051	    /// * [`safe_erc20::Error::SafeErc20FailedOperation`] - If transfer fails.
1052	    ///
1053	    /// # Events
1054	    ///
1055	    /// * [`Withdraw`]
1056	    pub fn _withdraw(
1057	        &mut self,
1058	        caller: Address,
1059	        receiver: Address,
1060	        owner: Address,
1061	        assets: U256,
1062	        shares: U256,
1063	        erc20: &mut Erc20,
1064	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
1065	        if caller != owner {
1066	            erc20._spend_allowance(owner, caller, shares)?;
1067	        }
1068	
1069	        // If asset() is ERC-777, `transfer` can trigger a reentrancy AFTER the
1070	        // transfer happens through the `tokens_received` hook. On the other
1071	        // hand, the `tokens_to_send` hook, that is triggered before the
1072	        // transfer, calls the vault, which is assumed not malicious.
1073	        //
1074	        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer after the burn so that any
1075	        // reentrancy would happen after the shares are burned and after the
1076	        // assets are transferred, which is a valid state.
1077	
1078	        erc20._burn(owner, shares)?;
1079	
1080	        self.safe_erc20.safe_transfer(self.asset(), receiver, assets)?;
1081	
1082	        self.vm().log(Withdraw { sender: caller, receiver, owner, assets, shares });
1083	
1084	        Ok(())
1085	    }

1090	    #[must_use]
1091	    pub fn _decimals_offset(&self) -> U8 {
1092	        self.decimals_offset.get()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Builds (or refreshes) the scratch crate used to check the erc20 module in
isolation while the rest of the crate is still being migrated.

The scratch crate only contains `utils` (snapshotted from the worktree, tests
stripped, a few call sites patched) and symlinks to the real
`token/erc20` and `token/common` directories of the worktree.
Nothing in the worktree is modified.
"""
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys

WT = "/tmp/bench/wt/erc20"
ISO = "/tmp/bench/exp/erc20-iso"
SRC = f"{ISO}/contracts/src"


def read(path):
    with open(path) as fh:
        return fh.read()


def write(path, text):
    with open(path, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(text)


def strip_tests(text):
    """Cuts the file at the first `#[cfg(test)]` line (tests are at the tail)."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() == "#[cfg(test)]":
            end = idx
            while end > 0 and lines[end - 1].lstrip().startswith("#["):
                end -= 1
            return "\n".join(lines[:end]).rstrip() + "\n"
    return text
